title: Beginner starting to develop a Real time grand strategy game, how do I get started?
author: apotheosis_0
selftext:
Hi guys, im a huge fan of paradox games, and recently I’ve been interested in developing a 2D grand-strategy game inspired by Hearts of Iron IV and Age of History III, but I noticed there’s not a lot of content regarding few time periods and also games that are in mobile that scratches the itch. Im a very creative but not technical guy. I have very little experience with game development or programming, but I’ve been working on the game’s design and mechanics and would now actually learn how to build the game properly.

Rn, I wanna keep it simple, so I want to build a prototype project just based off Europe.   
I’m considering Godot, but I’m open to other engines if there’s a compelling reason. My main focus is on the maps and provinces, with the buildings in them, as well frontlines by the army and how navy will be used. I intend to use AI coding assistants to help with development, but I also want to learn enough programming to understand the code, debug problems and maintain the project myself. Of course, all text, art, and music will be human generated.

Are there any existing tutorials, courses, open-source projects or examples of grand-strategy games that would be particularly useful?  
I’m not expecting to build the entire game immediately. I want to establish a sensible technical foundation and start with a small playable prototype. Any advice?

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: do things slowly and test. get a map, get a ui, get one unit online, then add things slowly and test. do small demos and then build a bigger game later. Outside of that get on youtube and watch some examples, your asking for alot in a reddit post

replies.body: Yeah, that’s the plan for now, to create a prototype. I just want to find a decent engine where I can build a game like the one I’m envisioning, and also if there’s tutorials online for it

comments.author: Arcodiant
comments.body:
I'd look at modding for those games first. The thing to realise for grand strategy is that you're not actually writing a grand strategy game directly; you're writing an engine on which the strategy game is built.

If you look at existing mods for the games you've mentioned, you'll see that they're largely building rules and content in a custom format/language for that game - it's all that logic that is then executed by the underlying engine to make the game happen.

replies.author: apotheosis_0
replies.body: Yep, I’ve seen tons of modding for those games, especially hearts of iron IV. They’re only good for the data and research they provide for the base game’s plot and world (ex. I don’t need to research the amount of population each province has because it’s already written in the game). Building a grand strategy game is more on building on the mechanics and creating a map and shaping each province, it’s definitely about writing an engine on which the strategy game is built

comments.author: PeerieCode
comments.body:
Godot is a good pick here, in my opinion. It’s free, light, and 2D is its strong side, so I wouldn’t switch engines for a prototype like this.

Since you want to use AI but also understand the code, here’s what I’d do:  
**Start tiny.** One small map, a few provinces, click to select, a clock you can pause and speed up. Armies and navy come after. Don’t build all of Europe first. Small steps make things more robust.  
**Ask AI to explain, not just write.** Build one small feature at a time and make the assistant explain every script. If you can’t say what it does, don’t add the next feature yet. It’s hard at the beginning, but over time you’ll learn a lot this way.
